summary: Harbin suits seasonal city travel shaped by European-style streets, river-edge openness, strong winter atmosphere, and hearty local food culture.
transport_notes: Harbin plans should stay clustered because cold-season travel and wide boulevards can make longer multi-stop days feel heavier.
Central areas work well with short rides plus walking, especially around major heritage streets and riverfront space.
Evening movement is strongest in central lit-up districts where dining and strolling stay compact.

budget_notes.low: Focus on central heritage streets, public riverfront areas, and practical local food without wide-area transfers.
budget_notes.medium: Combine one major street or landmark area, one river or park stop, and one stronger local dining area each day.
budget_notes.high: Use slower winter-friendly pacing, warmer dining breaks, and fewer long outdoor transitions.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans in Harbin should emphasize iconic streets, photogenic winter atmosphere, and practical local food value.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should balance broad city mood, reflective river walks, and manageable cold-weather pacing.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should use lights, snow-season atmosphere, and European-style street texture for memory-rich scenes.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should limit long outdoor exposure and keep warm-up breaks and landmark logic very clear.
